text: Mimi adopts a split residual vector quantization because a single 8‑level RVQ forces the first quantizer to sacrifice audio quality in order to gain phonetic discriminability, creating a conflict between reconstruction and semantic distillation losses【1】. By separating a plain VQ that receives the distilled semantic information from a parallel 7‑level RVQ that handles acoustic residuals, both streams can contribute to reconstruction without requiring the acoustic information to be preserved in the residual of the semantic quantizer【1】. This architecture improves the overall semantic‑acoustic trade‑off, raising MUSHRA scores while only modestly affecting ABX performance【4】.

answer:
Mimi adopts a split residual vector quantization because a single 8‑level RVQ forces the first quantizer to sacrifice audio quality in order to gain phonetic discriminability, creating a conflict between reconstruction and semantic distillation losses[1]. By separating a plain VQ that receives the distilled semantic information from a parallel 7‑level RVQ that handles acoustic residuals, both streams can contribute to reconstruction without requiring the acoustic information to be preserved in the residual of the semantic quantizer[1]. This architecture improves the overall semantic‑acoustic trade‑off, raising MUSHRA scores while only modestly affecting ABX performance[4].
